subject: Post-demo: OrchidHealth integration & private-connectivity plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chris Liu <chris.liu@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + next steps (SDK/auth/priv-connectivity)

Hi Chris — great demo earlier, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of what we covered
- Use case: patient intake triage + de-identified insights pipeline (low-PHI to start)
- Preferred topology from Orchid: private connectivity + strong auth controls; minimizing public egress for any PHI-related requests

Technical asks / items we need to confirm
1) Networking: you indicated Orchid prefers a VPC endpoint / PrivateLink-style onramp and IP-allowlist for API calls. We can support a VPC endpoint (Dedicated or Private deployment) with static egress + DNS override. Please confirm the egress model you want (NAT/static IP vs explicit proxy).
2) Auth: options: API key over private path, or mutual TLS client certs for Private deployments. Which is Orchid’s procurement preference?
3) Routing & structured output: do you want embeddings/reranker traffic routed to a separate dedicated pool (for isolation and billing)? We can route by model or route tag. Also want to confirm expected sequence length and typical request patterns for tool-calling / structured output to size KV cache properly.
4) Embeddings / re-rank: confirm whether you need embeddings to remain in your VPC (on-prem or Private deploy) or if hosting embeddings on Redwood Dedicated (with contractual isolation) is acceptable.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short integration playbook and a mutual action plan spreadsheet that map out the steps we usually follow (networking, PKI, procurement).

Proposed next steps (owners & ETA)
- Network touchpoint: Monica to schedule a call with your infra team to collect subnet/cidr/egress requirements (owner: Monica, ETA: 48 hours)
- Auth decision: Orchid to confirm API key vs mTLS (owner: Chris, ETA: 5 business days)
- Embeddings isolation: Orchid to indicate whether embeddings must run in-customer (owner: Chris/Alicia, ETA: 5 business days)
- Legal/procurement: Ben to kick off procurement thread once topology confirmed (owner: Ben, ETA: after network decision)

If you’d like, we can also provide a short network diagram showing our recommended VPC endpoint + DNS override flow.

Thanks — I’ll wait to hear which auth model you prefer and I’ll get Monica to schedule the network ping.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_integration_playbook.pdf (12 pages), orcid_mutual_action_plan.xlsx
From: Chris Liu <chris.liu@orchidhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Park <alicia@orchidhealth.com>, procurement@orchidhealth.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps (SDK/auth/priv-connectivity)

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Auth: Procurement will prefer mTLS for anything handling PHI; for non-PHI we could consider API key over a private endpoint. Does Redwood support client cert rotation (automated) or will we need to manage certs? Also need details on certificate lifetimes and revocation.

- Egress/DNS: We prefer that outbound traffic from our VPC to Redwood endpoints is via a VPC endpoint with NAT-provided static IPs on our side. Can Redwood accept inbound connections from our VPC endpoint or do we create a private peering? What DNS changes do you require (CNAMEs / private zone entries)?

- Embeddings/rerank: Our security lead asked whether embeddings can be computed inside our VPC (on a Private deployment) to avoid any egress. If not feasible immediately, can we at least ensure embeddings and rerank requests never leave the US region? Latency targets: we aim for sub-200ms tail for embeddings at small-batch sizes (N=8). Can you provide typical latencies for embeddings/rerank for the recommended model variants?

Looping procurement for timelines. Alicia — procurement question: if we go with a Private deployment + mTLS, what are typical lead times and costs?

Thanks — Chris
IT Security / Engineering
Orchid Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chris Liu <chris.liu@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps (SDK/auth/priv-connectivity)

Chris — thanks, good questions. Technical clarifications from our infra/solutions side below (I pulled Priyom into thread for infra sizing & latency numbers):

1) mTLS vs API key: 
- Redwood supports both. For Hosted API with a VPC onramp we typically use API key over a private path (IP allowlist + private DNS). For customers requiring PKI-level mutual auth we offer mTLS for Redwood Private deployments (customer-managed control plane or on-prem).
- Cert rotation: In Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for cert issuance/rotation. For our managed Private offering we provide an automated cert rotation job (we rotate client certs quarterly by default; can be shortened). We publish CRL endpoints and support OCSP.

2) Network topology & DNS: 
- Two supported patterns: 1) VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) where your VPC initiates traffic to Redwood private endpoint; 2) Private peering for Dedicated/Private when customer wants inbound access. Both support DNS override (private zone + CNAME to Redwood endpoint).
- If you need static egress IPs from your side for firewall rules we can also provide our egress IPs on Dedicated pools; otherwise routing through your NAT is fine. For Private deployments, all egress can be pinned to your control.

3) Embeddings & rerank latency/placement: 
- Option A (recommended for PHI): embeddings computed in-customer via Redwood Private on-prem or VPC-hosted Private. No external egress.
- Option B: embeddings on Redwood Dedicated in US-only region with contractual isolation / SOC2 + data-at-rest encryption; we can restrict model variants and ensure no cross-customer caching. Typical p50/p95 embeddings latency for our small-batch (N=8) on recommended model is ~45ms / 140ms respectively (network included depends on proximity). Rerank latency depends on candidate set size — with 25 candidates we typically see p95 ~220-350ms depending on model and rerank strategy. Priyom — attaching a short latency table in the playbook.

4) Structured output & function-calling: 
- Structured outputs (JSON schema enforcement) and tool-calling work the same across deployment types. For low-latency structured responses we recommend enabling KV prefix caching and a smaller model variant for rerank.

Next operational steps (owners & deadlines):
- Network kickoff: Monica to run a short network intake (CIDR, allowed ports, DNS zone) and hold a 30-min call with Orchid infra. ETA: EOD Wed (Monica).
- Infra sizing / latency table: Priyom to share recommended Dedicated/Private sizing and expected p95 numbers for embeddings/rerank. ETA: EOD Mon (Priyom).
- Procurement readiness: Ben to send draft order form & preliminary SOW once topology + auth are confirmed. ETA: after network decision.

Action items for Orchid to confirm: preferred auth model (API key vs mTLS), whether embeddings must run in-customer, and preferred timeline for go-live (PO target).

Attachments: same playbook + latency appendix.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: redwood_integration_playbook.pdf, latency_appendix.csv
